reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis creatively links two plausible but independently reported phenomena (nanosegregation and amorphization) into a single mechanistic framework, but the proposed mechanism of pre-existing Cr-rich precipitates curtailing fast nanosegregation is chemically counterintuitive and lacks a clear physical basis, making the overall chain of causality questionable.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is well-defined with clear groups, measurements, and a decisive falsification criterion, though the in situ TEM observation of amorphous nanobridge formation during fracture at 500–700°C is extremely challenging and may be impractical.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a critical engineering problem (intermediate-temperature embrittlement) with a novel, testable mechanism, and even if falsified, the experiment would generate valuable data on grain boundary engineering and crack-tip phenomena in HEAs.
